title: A wild man of the woods brought back from the Mississippi
summary: A Boston paper reported that a lumber company agent had returned from the St. Peters River on the upper Mississippi with a living wild man of the woods and two small cubs. The story ran in papers from North Carolina to Vermont.
hoax: A classic newspaper tall tale of its day; no such captive was ever exhibited.

title: The sea serpent returns to the Atlantic coast
summary: The Newport Herald of the Times said the sea serpent had been reported again along the coast, in Frenchman's Bay, off Nahant and as far south as Cape May. The editor admitted he had been sceptical, but was shaken when an old friend said he had seen it himself.

title: A hideous beast killed in the Illinois bottoms
place: Illinois River bottoms, fourteen miles west of Jerseyville
summary: Hunters in the Illinois River bottoms west of Jerseyville said they caught and killed a monster they could not decide was an animal or a reptile. It had a back like a skunk's and a rough brown belly.

title: A hairy wild man near Gallipolis
summary: The Gallipolis Bulletin reported a wild man in the woods near town: naked, covered in hair, very tall and with bulging eyes. Some older boys first saw him behind Carrell's Hill, and later he chased women along the Chillicothe road. The story was reprinted as far away as Vermont.

title: A strange animal caught near Farmville
summary: Two men near Farmville captured an animal no one there had seen before: about three feet long, slim and brown, with a small head, black eyes, long ears, a sharp nose and a long tail.

title: Cries from the Hurricane near Uniontown
place: The Hurricane, southwest of Uniontown, Kentucky
summary: The Uniontown Appeal said a family living near a tract of storm-felled forest called the Hurricane had for months heard cries like a child in distress coming from the timber. After long watching, the father finally saw a strange hairy creature there.
quote: a sight that made him creep

title: A 90-pound frog from a Tennessee cave
place: Indian Camp Spring, four miles south of Columbia, Tennessee
summary: A letter to the Columbia Herald, vouched for by a local man, said a giant frog weighing 90 pounds had been caught in a cave near Indian Camp Spring.
hoax: Has every mark of a frontier tall tale.

title: A porgy fisherman's serpent in Newark Bay
place: Newark Bay at Saltersville (Bayonne), New Jersey
summary: The Newark Courier vouched for James Andrews, a sober porgy fisherman from Saltersville on Newark Bay, who said he had seen the sea serpent. His neighbours generally believed him.
quote: not at all given to grog

title: A gorilla at large in Kansas
summary: A letter from Arcadia to the St. Louis Democrat said a wild man or gorilla had been seen at different times by nearly everyone in the valley, and occasionally across the line in Missouri, and had several times come close to houses. The story inspired Mark Twain's satirical "interview" with the wild man, which papers reprinted for months.
quote: It is nothing less than the discovery of a wild man or gorilla.

title: The monster snake of Pyramid Lake
summary: The Elko Independent said miners and prospectors had long passed on a Paiute story of a monster snake in Pyramid Lake, and that local Native people would not go near the water. The paper then gave a new account from men who said they had glimpsed it.

title: A wild man's den on the Big Sioux
place: Big Sioux River, Dakota side, northwest of Sioux City
summary: The Sioux City Times said a farmer hauling firewood on the Big Sioux saw what he took for a wild man bolt from a hollow log and outrun him into the woods. A mounted party found his den in a rock crevice lined with brush and animal skins. Reprints claimed he was a Frenchman who had fled into the wilds after a murder.

title: The Scottish Bride meets the serpent and its young
place: Reported on arrival at Delaware Bay (sighting at sea)
summary: Captain Allen of the bark Scottish Bride, arriving from Bordeaux, said he had passed the great sea serpent at sea, and that a smaller serpent swam with it. The New York Sun ran his description and it was copied from Minnesota to Nevada.
quote: The Sea Serpent still lives, and has an heir
hoax: The Sun's account was written with a wink.

title: A seven-foot bird screams in the treetops
summary: Boys out fox hunting near James Peoples' place outside Stanford heard unearthly screams from the treetops, along with what sounded like clanking chains, and fled. Papers later reported that a remarkable seven-foot bird had been captured there.

title: The mystic lights of the Auxvasse
place: Middle Auxvasse Creek, Callaway County, Missouri
summary: David Newsom wrote to the Fulton Gazette that his son Robert, riding alone one clear night near the Middle Auxvasse Creek, saw the countryside grow brighter until his mule stopped, part of a run of mysterious lights reported in the area.

title: A grave-robbing beast near Fostoria
summary: People in Perry Township, Wood County, were alarmed when an unknown animal burrowed into graves in the township cemetery, leaving claw marks and fur. Weeks later papers said the animal had been captured.

title: A sea monster bites an oar off Staten Island
summary: Eltingville was in an uproar after Constable Elbert Poillon said a sea serpent attacked his boat and crunched an oar. He described it as long as a shooting gallery, with a head like a powder keg. An oyster planter partly backed him up.
quote: a Head Like a Powder Keg

title: Six young men see the serpent off Grape Island
place: Between Grape Island and Hog Island, Essex County, Massachusetts
summary: The Georgetown Advocate said six young men sailing from Grape Island toward Hog Island saw something in the water they first took for seals chasing each other, then decided was the annual sea serpent.

title: Jacko, the British Columbia gorilla
place: Near Tunnel No. 4, above Yale, British Columbia
summary: American papers reprinted a story from Victoria's British Colonist: railway men near Tunnel No. 4, about twenty miles above Yale on the Fraser River, chased and captured a strange creature on the rock bluffs, half man and half beast. It became the famous Jacko story.
quote: Description of a Strange Creature Captured Near Yale.
hoax: Rival British Columbia papers soon reported that no such creature could be found, and most historians treat the story as a newspaper hoax.

title: A strange river monster chained on the Cumberland
summary: Two old fishermen caught a strange marine animal in the river above the Nashville waterworks and kept it staked and chained by the tail to the bank until it could be put on show near the square.

title: The phantom beacon over the Marine City wreck
summary: The Detroit Post told of a mysterious light that people along the Lake Huron shore said appeared over the wreck of the steamer Marine City, which burned off Harrisville a few years earlier.

title: A huge buzzing bird over a Carson ranch
place: Road from Carson City to Genoa, Nevada
summary: A farmer on the Genoa road heard a strange noise in the air at midnight and saw what looked like a huge bird hovering over his ranch, giving off a buzzing sound. He fetched his shotgun.

title: An eagle caught in a fox trap
summary: Lewis Williams set a fox trap in the mountains near Stockport and found an eagle had dragged it away. He tracked the bird down and had a fierce fight before he overpowered it.

title: A tug captain's Lake Michigan monster
place: Lake Michigan, later off Death's Door, Wisconsin
summary: A tug captain, Dick Brewer, said a large black monster surfaced ahead of his boat as he towed a mud scow past the Marine Hospital, setting off talk among sailors. Fishermen later reported it again off Death's Door.

title: A circus jaguar loose near Enon
summary: When Barret's circus train was stopped by a burned railroad bridge near Enon, a jaguar escaped from its cage unnoticed. It ran across the countryside, stampeding and killing cattle, and the story ran in thirteen papers.

title: A monster in Lake Kampeska, Dakota
place: Lake Kampeska, near Watertown, Dakota Territory
summary: Workmen building a steamer on Lake Kampeska had already reported a huge animal, and been laughed at, when four men on shore watched something about 20 feet long, like a log, cross the lake faster than the steamer could go, circle and sink. Some suggested a giant sturgeon trapped in the lake.

title: Four campers at Rockport stop doubting
place: Off Gally Point, near the Rockport breakwater, Massachusetts
summary: A Gloucester lawyer, a police-court clerk, a bank teller and a friend camping at Gally Point said a serpent over 100 feet long and as thick as a barrel swam within 200 yards of them one Saturday evening. All four had been unbelievers.

title: A serpent in the Hudson chases two rowers
place: Hudson River off Kingston Point, New York
summary: Boatmen, swimmers and a schooner captain said a huge serpent raised its head six feet out of the Hudson near Kingston Point, with a fin running down its back. Over the next days it was reported again, once chasing two young men in a rowboat to the far shore.
quote: they were all perfectly sober

title: A sailing party meets the serpent off Gloucester
summary: An old sailor, the president of Gloucester's council, a customs officer and a sea captain said they sailed within a few hundred feet of what looked like a floating spar nearly 100 feet long. Then a huge head rose with two glittering eyes, and the thing sank and surfaced again farther off.

title: A child-sized 'what is it' hunting frogs
place: Woods along the river near Mexico, Wyandot County, Ohio
summary: Several people near Sycamore described an animal the size of a four- or five-year-old child when it stood up, with monkey-like feet, short reddish-brown hair, a flat nose, fox ears and big fangs. They said it hunted frogs on the riverbank by day, and its cry sounded like a child and a wolf at once.

title: Fifty people watch the serpent off Pigeon Cove
summary: On a calm, sunny afternoon about fifty people, among them two Boston school principals and a music professor, watched through glasses as something about 80 feet long moved north for twenty minutes, showing ten to fifteen humps at once. A school of porpoises passed at the same time, and witnesses said the two looked nothing alike.

title: A horned, rainbow-scaled monster at Lake Mazaska
place: Lake Mazaska, Shieldsville Township, Rice County, Minnesota
summary: A Faribault man driving home along Lake Mazaska said a 30-foot animal with two long horns and scales that flashed yellow, blue and green swam toward him, then rose on its hind feet and walked into the road. A postmaster and a fishing party had reported it two weeks before.

title: Two salesmen see Champ from a hotel porch
summary: Two travelling salesmen from Albany and Troy, sitting on the veranda of the Fouquet House, saw the calm bay suddenly churn 200 feet out. Part of a huge, arched, porpoise-shaped body at least 100 feet long showed for a moment, and both said they became believers.

title: A 40-foot snake in the Buzzard Den cave
place: The Buzzard Den cave on Big Two Mile Creek, east of Milton, West Virginia
summary: Melzar Braley, about twenty, said he heard a sheep bleating from a cave on Big Two Mile Creek and found a black-and-yellow striped serpent about 40 feet long swallowing it. He rolled a boulder down on it, and it let the sheep go and slid out of the cave hissing. Men gathered later heard it but did not see it.

title: Something lifts a rowboat in the Connecticut River
summary: Colonel Stocking and Silas Sage said that while they rowed across the river their boat was struck from below and lifted nearly out of the water. They then saw a serpent close to 100 feet long with its head ten feet up, churning off upriver. A professor at Middletown doubted it, and Stocking wrote to the papers to defend his story.

title: A Navy lieutenant sees a serpent off 27th Street
place: Hudson (North) River off 27th Street, Manhattan, New York
summary: Lieutenant G. A. Foster of the training ship Minnesota said he watched a dull grey, eel-like animal at least 60 feet long swim slowly up the Hudson from the 27th Street pier. His quartermaster followed it through a marine glass and backed up every detail.
quote: he hadn't had anything to drink for over a week

title: A seven-foot beast that leaps thirty feet
summary: For weeks people around Middlebourne reported glimpses of an animal at least seven feet long, something like a grey fox, that could leap thirty feet and left only light tracks. The paper reporting it couldn't decide whether it was a lion or a lie.

title: A 50-foot monster crosses San Diego Bay
place: San Diego Bay off the 22nd Street depot, California
summary: At sunset the freight agent's wife at the 22nd Street depot screamed for her husband, and four people watched something about 50 feet long with a head like a giant bullhead and a fish's tail race across the rough bay toward National City.

title: A serpent off Westport mistaken for porpoises
place: Long Island Sound between Westport and Southport, Connecticut
summary: Three men out sailing from Westport took what they saw for a school of porpoises until they got close. They said a serpent held its head five feet up and showed 70 to 100 feet of body, then half sank and sped off, leaving a wake like a steamboat's.

title: A 'gorilla' in the woods at Setauket
summary: After a farmer's prize sheep and a neighbour's hens were found torn apart, a Setauket farmer said his horses shied at a big ape about five feet tall standing upright at the edge of a swamp, holding a sapling. Farmers took guns to the fields and children were walked to school.

title: A hairy wild man chases hunters in Holmes County
place: Near Big Spring and Killbuck Creek, northern Holmes County, Ohio
summary: Four armed pheasant hunters said a naked man covered in matted hair ran at them from a thicket, making strange guttural sounds, and chased them to the road. It then dropped onto all fours, plunged into Killbuck Creek and swam it like a dog.

title: A streak of foam racing down Lake Champlain
place: Lake Champlain east of Willsboro Point, New York
summary: Five men at Willsboro Point, all of them doubters until then, watched a dark body at the head of a long streak of foam race south down the lake against the wind, throwing spray twenty feet in the air. Through a spyglass they followed it nearly as far as Essex and guessed its speed at a mile a minute.

title: A bushy-tailed 'varmint' raids Anderson County farms
place: Near Deep Creek Grange Hall, Anderson County, South Carolina
summary: A dark animal with erect ears and a bushy tail, "very much like a dog", ate a pup, tried to get in through a farmhouse door and tore the ears and face off a pig in one night. The paper's correspondent was shown the mangled pig and the tracks.

title: A copper-coloured killer of calves in Bartow County
place: Farms near Cartersville, Bartow County, Georgia
summary: Sheep, hogs and calves were found dead with only a small stab-like wound under the throat. A farmer hiding in his corn lot at dawn shot at a dark copper animal with a sharp, possum-like head and bead eyes as it crept, cat-like, up to a sleeping calf. It vanished, and armed bands searched for it.

title: A 25-foot snake with a hairy head at Thunder Bay
place: Farms along Thunder Bay near Alpena, Michigan
summary: A farmer found a foot-wide trail across his ploughed field to the bay, and his son, planting potatoes, fired twice at a black, yellow-spotted snake about 25 feet long with long black hair on its head. It went off as fast as a horse into the bay, and hair eight inches long was found where it passed under a fence.

title: Four sailors see a serpent near Simcoe Island
place: St. Lawrence River near Simcoe Island, opposite Cape Vincent, New York
summary: Four men sailing from Wolfe Island said they saw a serpent about 80 feet long near Simcoe Island. Across the river in Cape Vincent the lawyer, customs collector and town supervisor debated the story at the post office, and three men set off to try to catch it.

title: An alligator-headed serpent off Point Judith
place: Two miles southwest of Point Judith, Rhode Island
summary: Two experienced sailors on a sloop said a head like an alligator's, with five-foot jaws, long teeth and eyes as big as a hat crown, passed within ten feet of them, with a stiff fin down its back and a body at least 70 feet long. It followed reports of a serpent off Watch Hill.

title: A steamer captain studies a serpent in Georgetown harbour
place: Georgetown harbour, between the port and the bar, South Carolina
summary: The captain of the steamer Planter said a tug passed within 200 yards of a dark, resting serpent about 50 feet long with a beak-like mouth and large oval head. Woken by the noise, it threw its tail into the air and made for the mud flats of Muddy Bay where the tug couldn't follow.

title: A maned serpent off the Umpqua River
place: Pacific Ocean off the mouth of the Umpqua River, Oregon
summary: The captain of the coal bark Estrella, with his wife and crew watching, said an 80-foot serpent as thick as a barrel swam by 200 yards off with its head and ten feet of neck raised, the neck covered in coarse hair like a mane. He fired his rifle at it; the shots fell short.

title: A horned black beast in the Great Bear Swamp
summary: Farmers around the Great Bear Swamp lost sheep and hogs two winters running, finding only oddly shaped tracks. The one witness, a hired man the paper called of doubtful veracity, said it was a big black monster with horns, twice the size of a sheep. A Thanksgiving hunt was planned.

title: An unknown night beast at White Sulphur
summary: Something seen only at night around White Sulphur attacked dogs and bit a farmer's fat hogs, which died showing signs of rabies. Those who glimpsed it called it a hyena, a tiger or a wildcat, and dogs refused to leave the houses.

title: A giant snake rears up in Twin Lakes
summary: A fisherman from South Egremont, Massachusetts, said what he took for a blackened stump in 75 feet of water moved, left a wake and reared a flat, two-foot head six feet out of the lake, with a body ten to twelve inches thick.

title: A serpent in the Sacramento overflow
place: The overflow east of Pritchard's Lake, near Pleasant Grove, California
summary: Ranchers around Pleasant Grove, north of Sacramento, said a serpent over 40 feet long was seen in the flood overflow near Pritchard's Lake, and on land too. The keeper of a duck-shooting club on the lake said he had found strange tracks and lost many chickens.

title: Five anglers rocked by the Fish Trap Lake monster
place: Fish Trap Lake, below Galena, Illinois
summary: Five men trolling on Fish Trap Lake, below Galena, said the calm water suddenly boiled and their boat heaved and rocked as a huge serpent-like fish surfaced. They linked it to a similar monster reported there about ten years before.

title: A serpent lassoed off Brant Rock
summary: A father and son out in a boat off Brant Rock said they chased a long, snake-like animal and got a rope around its head while a crowd watched from the beach. A second man rowed out, and the two fired charge after charge into its head with little effect as it towed them along.

title: A strange creature prowls a Chicago suburb
summary: A Chicago suburb was in a fright after rumours of a bear or similar animal grew into the traditional wild man. Two young men described a thrilling encounter, and searches came up empty.

title: Coon hunters kill a mystery beast in Henry County
summary: After weeks of crippled and killed livestock and a man chased by an animal bigger than a big dog, coon hunters' hounds ran down a beast. The men finished it with stones and an axe. It was five feet three inches long, and they called it a "Mexican lion", likely a cougar.

title: A rolling ball of fire near Coatesville
place: Half a mile south of Coatesville, Missouri, near the Chariton River
summary: Every evening around nine a light like a train's headlight rolled across the railroad near Coatesville, rose fifty feet, stopped in an old orchard and graveyard and sank into the ground. As many as fifty people watched it at once. Spiritualists blamed the dead in the graveyard.

title: A wild man who lives on grass
place: Mountain View, Passaic County, New Jersey
summary: The mountain hamlet of Mountain View in Passaic County was alarmed by a wild man in the woods who was said to live on grass. Hunting parties searched the woods in every direction.

title: A dragon on the Flat Rock derrick
summary: The Mexico Weekly Ledger reported great commotion in Flat Rock at midnight when an unearthly winged creature with a gorilla-like head, horns and long shaggy arms was said to have landed on top of a high derrick and switched its forked tail.
hoax: Written as comedy by the local paper.

title: A gorilla in the hills around Vernon
summary: The Cincinnati Enquirer reported a gorilla-like creature in the rugged hills around Vernon, Indiana, near a cavern a local man claimed to have found years earlier. The paper wondered if it was Darwin's missing link.
quote: Perhaps This Is Darwin's Long-Sought Missing Link

title: A wild man caught on Salado Creek
place: Salado Creek near San Antonio, Texas
summary: A farmer near San Antonio said that after a long chase he captured a wild man on Salado Creek, with a foot-long shaggy black beard, hair down his back and nails three inches long. The Ocala Banner said it revived an old Florida wild-man scare.

title: The ten-cent wild man was a fake
summary: Local showmen in Salt Lake City exhibited a captured wild man for ten cents until Sheriff Burt tugged at his eyebrows and found they were glued on.
quote: The Eyebrows Were Stuck on the Wild Man.
hoax: An exhibit fraud, exposed by the sheriff.

title: An old tale of an eight-foot hairy giant in Georgia
summary: A widely reprinted 1891 item retold an old account of hunters in the Rabun County mountains finding a being nearly eight feet tall, covered in hair, with a human face and huge ears like a donkey's.
hoax: A retold legend, not a contemporary sighting.

title: The beacon keeper fights a sea monster
place: Greenport breakwater, Long Island, New York
summary: Captain Edward Reeve, who rowed out each evening to light the beacon on the Greenport breakwater and was known as a sober, reliable man, told the New York World he had fought off a sea monster from his skiff.

title: The Capay Valley what-is-it
place: Mountains at the head of Capay Valley, Yolo County, California
summary: For weeks, Yolo County papers ran yarns about a freak of nature in the mountains at the head of Capay Valley, nicknamed the What-is-It. Two more men then said they had followed the creature to its lair.
hoax: The Sacramento paper said the story may have been started deliberately.

title: The dragons of Fresno
summary: A St. Louis Republic story said reputable citizens in a Fresno County farming district swore they had seen and hunted two dragons with fifteen-foot wings and featherless bodies, which seized fowls with three snaps of their jaws.
quote: Winged Monsters That Devour Fowls with Three Snaps of Their Jaws
hoax: Has all the marks of a newspaper tall tale.

title: A seven-headed serpent comes up the Santa Cruz
place: Santa Cruz River below Tucson, Arizona
summary: The Arizona Weekly Citizen ran a comic account of a seven-headed sea serpent that came up the dry Santa Cruz River below Tucson, watched by frightened hundreds, and delivered a sermon and prophecy.
hoax: Pure newspaper comedy; the Santa Cruz is usually dry.

title: A wild man runs through Southwest City
summary: Southwest City was thrown into excitement when a man taken for a maniac came rushing through the streets, frightening everyone, and was captured after a hard struggle. Stranger stories about him followed.

title: An eagle and a child at Echo Lake
place: Echo Lake near Sault Ste. Marie, Michigan
summary: A dispatch from Sault Ste. Marie said a Chippewa guide setting out from his home on Echo Lake saw an enormous bald eagle circling, and the paper reported that the bird killed his baby daughter, who had been left outside the door.

title: Gloucester fishermen meet a serpent on the Flemish Cap
place: Reported at Gloucester; seen on the Flemish Cap fishing bank
summary: Gloucester fishermen back from the distant Flemish Cap bank said a sea serpent over 80 feet long, resembling a giant squid, appeared while they were hauling their trawls, and that a marine monster wrecked trawl lines and overturned dories.

title: A wild man run down in the Hayward hills
place: Eden Township hills near Haywards and Dublin, California
summary: Hunters and farmers in the hills of Eden Township near Haywards and Dublin had glimpsed a creature that ran like a deer. A Haywards constable finally caught him, a man who had been living wild and eating quail, and brought him to the county jail.

title: Hunters catch the wild man of the Okaw
summary: For two weeks, people along Beck's Creek in Loudon Township were worried by a supposed wild man who roamed the Okaw River bottoms living on young pigs and calves. A party of hunters finally captured him.

title: The Lake Kenosia serpent is captured
summary: Danbury announced that the famous Lake Kenosia serpent had been caught. Warren Baker, driving along the shore, saw what he took for a big tree limb across the road until his horse shied. The creature was said to be almost twenty feet long and covered with scales.
hoax: The Sun printed it in its usual playful style; no specimen was ever described by a scientist.

title: The wild man of Long Valley, Idaho
place: Mountains around Long Valley, Boise County, Idaho
summary: A sheepherder hid in a tree and watched a man with knee-length matted brown hair, in tattered overalls, kill a grouse with a thrown stick and eat it raw. Chased on horseback, he outran the horse over the rocks. Papers suspected an escaped asylum patient.

title: The Cedar Bass Lake monster
place: Bass Lake (Cedar Bass Lake), southeast of Knox, Indiana
summary: After years of torn nets, a capsized rowboat and a steamer tugged by its anchor line, a fishing party from Knox (including the lawyer who had defended President Garfield's assassin) hooked something that ran out a thousand feet of line. Passengers on the little steamer City of Kokomo said the animal surged up under the bow and nearly swamped them.

title: Provincetown fishermen kill a 'sea serpent'
summary: Weir fishermen found their fish trap churning yellow and a mass of dark ridges filling it: a single eel-shaped animal nearly thirty feet long, which they killed after a fight. Papers announced the sea serpent captured; it was most likely a large shark or other fish.

title: The steamer Edith meets a serpent in Puget Sound
place: Off Marrowstone Point, Puget Sound, Washington
summary: Crew and passengers of the steamer Edith watched for nearly half an hour as a head like a huge snake's, as big as a man's body, rose five feet out of the water off Marrowstone Point, turning from side to side and opening its mouth. It dived and came up on the other side of the boat.

title: A seven-foot hairy 'half man' near Olathe
place: Along Cedar Creek near Olathe, Johnson County, Kansas
summary: People along Cedar Creek described a naked creature about seven feet tall covered in brown hair, standing stooped with its long arms crossed and moving fast with a swinging gait. One man said it chased him for a mile, a dairy farmer blamed it for two dead cows and a calf, and an armed party searched the woods.

title: A snake as thick as a man across the road
place: Near Circleville, Orange County, New York
summary: Two boys walking near Circleville took a log across the road for a log until it glistened, brown, yellow and white, and began to move. A neighbour said a huge snake had lived in a cave near his place for years, and men organized a hunt.

title: A tug captain slows for a monster off Sodus Point
place: Lake Ontario off Sodus Point, New York
summary: Returning from a fishing trip with railroad officials, the captain of the tug Cornelia felt the boat roll and saw a huge object moving alongside at half the tug's speed. He rang to slow down for a better look, and it dived into water forty or fifty fathoms deep.

title: A feathered monster shot in Lincoln County
place: Mouth of Vannatters Creek near Hamlin, West Virginia
summary: Elias Midkiff of Hamlin asked the West Virginia historical society to send a taxidermist for a monster bird, unlike anything seen in the state, that W. W. Adkins had killed with five rifle bullets at the mouth of Vannatters Creek. The item was reprinted from Kansas to Oregon.
quote: a kind never seen before by anyone in West Virginia

title: Tug crews pass a 75-foot serpent
place: Long Island Sound off Saybrook Point, Connecticut
summary: Crews of the tugs Runyon and Aries, heading east past Saybrook Point, reported a sea serpent at least 75 feet long that stayed in sight for ten minutes before it disappeared.

papers.paper: The Daily Morning Journal and Courier

title: A sea serpent frozen off Currituck
summary: A North Carolina paper reported, with plenty of jokes about President Cleveland's recent duck hunt, that a sea serpent had been found frozen to death off the Currituck coast.
hoax: Written tongue in cheek.

title: A giant wild man near Cape Flattery
place: Quillayute country near Cape Flattery, Washington
summary: Lawrence F. Doyle, a Montana legislator, said that while crossing unexplored timber near Cape Flattery he closely watched a hatless wild man of unusually large size, with a heavy beard and a shock of long hair. He offered to swear affidavits. The item ran in papers from Georgia to Oregon.
quote: A sure enough wild man was seen in the Quillayute Mountains

title: The phantom goat of Hell Creek
place: Rocky Ford road, three miles west of New Albany, Mississippi
summary: Travellers crossing the dark creek bottoms three miles west of New Albany told the same story: a monster white goat rearing up on its hind legs in the road, as if to attack horse and rider. The stream had been nicknamed Hell Creek.
quote: All the Mississippians Who Have Seen It Tell the Same Story.

title: A 75-foot carcass on a Seattle dock
summary: The Seattle Post-Intelligencer described a midnight crowd staring at a huge bluish mass, said to be 75 feet long, that the sea had thrown up and that had sunk half a dock under its weight.
hoax: Printed on April 1; it reads like an April Fool's story.

title: A huge black eagle kills a calf
summary: Hall Revercomb said a huge black eagle had killed or maimed more than a dozen of his sheep. He set out to kill it after watching it swoop down and kill a calf.

title: The wild man of the great swamp
place: Great swamp near Vineland and Waterford, New Jersey
summary: Farmers on the edge of a great swamp in South Jersey reported a tall wild man with a mass of hair and beard, wearing moccasins and carrying a club, who taunted searchers with cries. Residents of Waterford caught him a few days later; he escaped, was cornered again and locked up. He turned out to be a mentally ill man who had been living in the woods.
quote: He leads his pursuers a fast chase

title: Fishermen kill a horned sea monster
summary: Captain Shannon and his crew fought a strange fish for two hours off the New Jersey coast and killed it: about 15 feet long and 500 pounds, with a horn on its nose, two rows of teeth and silvery armour-like scales. No fisherman there could say what it was.
quote: the like of which none of the fishermen had ever seen

title: The lighthouse keeper's serpent
summary: John Skipworth, keeper of the new light at the end of the Saybrook jetty, said he watched a monstrous sea serpent playing on the surface of Long Island Sound one Sunday afternoon, and guessed it at hundreds of feet long. His wife and a ship's captain were said to back him up.

papers.paper: The Daily Morning Journal and Courier.

title: A monster snake in the woods near Denver, Indiana
summary: Eric Gustin said that while driving home at dusk with his wife and another woman, their horse nearly collapsed with fright at a monster snake in the woods east of town. The story was reprinted for months, from Scranton to Idaho.
quote: This Snake May Be the Sea Serpent on a Land Voyage.

title: A vulture as tall as a man
summary: The superintendent of Richard Gird's ranch caught a California vulture (condor) in the hills south of Chino after it had gorged on a dead cow and was too full to fly. The paper said it stood six feet tall, an inch or two taller than its captor.
quote: A bird of prey as tall as a man!

title: Tacoma fishermen bring in a sea serpent
summary: Two Tacoma fishermen said they caught a live sea serpent in Puget Sound: smooth-skinned, spotted like a tiger, about 17 feet long by one account. Later reports spoke of two smaller ones from Hood Canal, eight and ten feet long, put on show in Tacoma. A Kansas paper ran the story under the headline that the monster was not a myth.
quote: Has a Bulldog's Head, a Tiger's Fangs, a Snake's Body

title: Two hundred people see a serpent off Lighthouse Point
summary: On a Sunday afternoon, more than 200 people at Lighthouse Point in New Haven said a 100-foot sea serpent, about fourteen feet around, swam close past several pleasure boats and headed for deep water. The paper joked that the Sunday liquor laws ruled out the usual explanation.
quote: Have you seen the sea serpent?

papers.paper: The Daily Morning Journal and Courier.

title: Minot's wild man
summary: Half a dozen people near Minot said they saw a ragged, heavily whiskered wild man close up in broad daylight before he vanished into the woods. Weeks later he appeared to a South Auburn farmer carrying a long butcher knife, and a woman from Aroostook County came forward thinking he might be her missing husband.
quote: Like all wild men he has more whiskers than clothes.

title: A lobsterman's monster in Plum Cove
summary: William Henry Sargent was hauling lobster pots off Lanesville when he saw a sea monster, rowed ashore in a fright and gathered a crowd. Everyone watching agreed it was about 80 feet long before it disappeared.

title: A barge captain's serpent at Stratford Shoals
place: Stratford Shoals, mouth of the Housatonic, Connecticut
summary: Captain Ewing of South Amboy, towing coal barges up the Housatonic, told people at the Derby docks that he had seen a big sea serpent off Stratford Shoals. The paper vouched that he was an honest old salt who did not drink enough to affect his sight.

title: High jinks at Lake Ripley
summary: A Chicago Tribune piece said the Lake Ripley serpent was snatching sheep, swallowing calves and chickens, cracking the winter ice and tossing the swimmers' diving floats around.
hoax: Written as summer-resort comedy.

title: Anglers spot a serpent off Throgg's Neck
place: Off Throgg's Neck, Long Island Sound, New York
summary: Two Whitestone anglers, Anthony Rick and Wesley Hunt, said a sea serpent went scurrying through the water off Throgg's Neck, apparently headed for New York. Days later other boaters described a green monster about fifty feet long in the Sound.

papers.paper: The Daily Morning Journal and Courier

title: The Provincetown sea serpent was a turtle
summary: Captain Richard Horton of the fishing schooner Minnehaha was said to have captured the sea serpent off Provincetown. It turned out to be a large loggerhead turtle that put up a hard fight.
hoax: Explained at the time: a loggerhead turtle.

title: A 49-foot serpent on the Carrabelle wharf
summary: A dispatch from Carrabelle said a sea serpent 49 feet long, eel-shaped with a spoonbill head and forked tongue, was killed in the Gulf after towing the steamer Crescent City for an hour, and was lying on the town wharf. The story travelled to Washington, Savannah, Wichita and beyond.
hoax: No specimen was ever examined by a scientist; it has the marks of a newspaper tall tale.

title: A naked man running wild near Annaton
summary: Several people near Annaton in Grant County reported a man with no clothes running wild through the woods and brush along the roads. The sheriff went out to investigate.

title: The Rock Lake monster fights back
summary: A Watertown paper said fishermen had long reported a huge serpent or water beast in Rock Lake that broke their lines. A Chicago alderman said he had battled it and that it had feet and scales like an alligator, and an old resident claimed it once towed his boat for several rods.

title: Rumours of a wild man on the Hudson
summary: For weeks, women and children in Irvington-on-the-Hudson said a wild man in tattered clothes was lurking in the woods along Hartman Lane, near a railroad agent's house.

title: A horse-headed thing in the Columbia
place: Columbia River near Clifton, Clatsop County, Oregon
summary: Dominick Bule, a salmon fisherman at Clifton, said that at dusk a huge animal rose out of the Columbia twenty feet from his boat. It had a hairy, horse-like head and four tusks a foot long, and stared at him for about two minutes.

title: A bright light crosses Sacramento
summary: On a Tuesday evening, hundreds of people in Sacramento watched a brilliant white light drift over the east side of the city, rising and falling as it went. Some witnesses insisted they saw a dark body behind the light and heard voices aboard. This was the opening night of the great 1896-97 airship wave.
quote: It was cigar shaped.

title: The mayor's men see it over the ocean
summary: San Francisco mayor Adolph Sutro said employees at his Sutro Heights estate watched a dark mass with two lights come in over the ocean at about 500 feet, sweeping a searchlight-like beam, then turn north toward the city. Sutro said he believed an inventor had solved aerial navigation.
quote: these people would not try to tell me ghost stories

title: A lawyer says his client built the airship
summary: San Francisco attorney George D. Collins told reporters that a wealthy client had built a working airship and flown it over Sacramento, and promised a public exhibition. Papers then named a dentist, Dr. E. H. Benjamin, as the secret inventor. Collins soon backed away from his story, and no airship or inventor was ever produced.
hoax: Collins retracted much of what he was quoted as saying, and the New-York Tribune called the whole affair one of the strangest hoaxes in the country.

title: The light returns to Sacramento
summary: Days after the first sighting, crowds in Sacramento again watched a large white light move quickly across the evening sky toward the southwest. One man driving a streetcar said his passengers made him stop so they could get out and stare.
quote: the most uncanny looking thing I ever saw

title: Seen heading for Mount Hamilton
summary: A young San Jose man, Frank Everett, said he watched the airship pass high over the eastern part of the city at about 11 at night, moving toward Mount Hamilton and its observatory. Others on Santa Clara Street said they saw it too.

title: Streetcar riders see an airship shaped like a bird
summary: Passengers on a streetcar near Oakland watched a light in the direction of Haywards and said they could make out the outline of a craft shaped like a huge bird, throwing a beam of light ahead of it. Oakland residents talked of little else and guessed the machine was hidden somewhere in Alameda County.
quote: The ship resembles a huge bird in its outlines

title: Telephone workers watch a light head for Gilroy
summary: Three employees of the Sunset Telephone company in San Jose reported a bright light moving rapidly across the sky at about 11 p.m., heading south toward Gilroy. Two nights later more San Jose residents described lights passing over the city.

title: Market Street crowd stares at a star
summary: At about 6 p.m. the cry went up on Market Street that the airship's headlight was visible high over the city, and excited crowds gathered to watch. A professor who checked with his telescope said the supposed airship was an ordinary star.
hoax: A professor identified the light as a star.

title: Santa Rosa sees a light with wings
summary: Airship fever reached Santa Rosa when a bright light appeared at 7:30 p.m. and hundreds of people went out to watch. It seemed to move east, vanishing with a dull red glow and then reappearing, and some were ready to swear it had huge wings.

title: The airship crosses the Tehachapis
summary: Los Angeles papers reported that the famous airship had apparently crossed the Tehachapi range, after a book dealer and two other residents described a moving light. Within days, people up late in the San Fernando Valley described strange lights near the hills on three nights running.

title: Rising out of a canyon near Haywards
summary: A Haywards man named Mohr said he watched the airship rise from a canyon near his place, fly toward San Francisco and come back, and believed it was kept near Lone Tree Cemetery. Three well-known Haywards citizens gave their own account of the same lights.

title: Coloured flashes near Mount Tacoma
summary: Several people in Tacoma said they saw the airship near Mount Tacoma (Mount Rainier), giving off flashes of different colours. They guessed the inventor had built a second machine, or had taken an evening spin up from California.

title: Nevada men say they saw it weeks earlier
summary: After reading the California stories, two Silver City men said they had seen the same airship about six weeks before, though at the time they took it for a meteor or a comet.

title: Pat Nunan's ride in the sky
summary: In a Sacramento saloon, a man named Pat Nunan entertained the stove-side crowd with a long account of being lured aboard the airship and taken for a ride. The paper printed it as a comic yarn.
hoax: Told and printed as a saloon yarn.

title: Two lights over the Sierra foothills
summary: Around the time the airship was said to have flown south, people at Robinson's Ferry in Calaveras County reported two mysterious lights moving high over the mountains.

title: An electrician's close-up view
summary: Case Gibson, a young Oakland electrician and the son of a school superintendent, told reporters he had seen the airship at close range and gave a detailed description of it in flight. Students at Stanford also reported a light they took for the airship.

title: Fishermen say they dined with the aeronauts
place: Beach north of Pacific Grove, Monterey County, California
summary: Two Pacific Grove fishermen said an airship about sixty feet long and made of metal landed on the beach some fifteen miles north of town, and that they talked and ate with its three crewmen. The paper sent a correspondent to look for evidence.
hoax: No evidence of a landing was reported; it reads as a tall tale.

title: A Fresno barkeeper meets the inventor
summary: George Jennings, part owner of the bar at Fresno's Grand Central Hotel, said a stranger came in claiming to be the airship's inventor and told him the craft had been caught by an air current and was now somewhere in Fresno County.

title: A tin airship falls into a gulch
summary: A San Francisco story, reprinted in Kansas, said a 40-foot airship of galvanised sheet steel sailed over Twin Peaks, lost control and plunged into a gulch near the Corbett road, bruising its two crewmen. Reporters described its twisted propeller.
hoax: A homemade contraption or a newspaper stunt; nothing like it flew in 1896.

title: Flying machines in flocks
summary: Mysterious lights floated over Oakland and Alameda one night, one shooting up over Piedmont and drifting into the clouds, followed by others. A Washington paper reprinted the story under a joking headline about airships appearing in flocks.
hoax: The papers treated it as a joke; such lights were often paper fire balloons sent up by pranksters.

title: The catawampus of Doe Gully tunnel
place: Doe Gully tunnel, B&O Railroad, near the Potomac
summary: Railroad men reported a strange beast near Doe Gully tunnel on the Baltimore and Ohio line that killed a mountain farmer's sheep. A railroad official said he saw it come down to the river to drink. Seven hunters saw it but could not get a shot, and men went to the fields armed. Locals called it the catawampus.
quote: men go to and from their work in the fields armed

title: Prayer-meeting crowd hears voices from the sky
summary: Inavale residents said the airship already reported near Hastings had been seen over their town several times. On a dark night, ten or twelve people coming home from prayer meeting described a cone-shaped craft thirty to forty feet long and said they heard voices. It was one of the first reports of the 1897 Midwestern wave.
quote: Thirty to Forty Feet Long and Conical in Shape

title: Telegraph operators watch for the Kansas airship
summary: From Atchison came word that the supposed Kansas airship had been seen in Nebraska, and that railroad telegraph operators across northern Kansas spent the night watching for it.

title: A winged ship ablaze with light over Ellinwood
summary: Ellinwood citizens described an immense airship moving south at about forty miles an hour, with two huge wings or propellers on each side and a rudder at the back. It was lit from stem to stern and stayed in view for about ten minutes. The paper noted that Ellinwood was a dry town.
quote: The ship was one blaze of light from stem to stern

title: A ball of fire crosses Omaha
summary: On a Monday night, large numbers of Omaha people saw a big light pass over the city in a way that suggested someone was steering it. A citizen of North Loup wrote in to say the light had come from his direction. The excitement lasted all week.

title: Scores of Belleville people see it under control
summary: The airship sighted around Kansas and southern Nebraska for a month passed over Belleville several times in one week, and many residents watched it. They believed it was the same machine first reported in California and that someone was steering it.

title: Omaha sees it for the third time
summary: On a Sunday evening, reputable Omaha citizens watched the mysterious light for the third time, visible for about half an hour as it hovered over the city. Nearly every paper in the Midwest carried the dispatch.

title: Kansas City swears to the strange lights
summary: On April Fools' Day, many respectable citizens of Kansas City, Kansas, solemnly declared they had seen the strange lights at 8 p.m., and the papers printed an affidavit. Two nights later, thousands in Kansas City said the visitor came back.
quote: Notwithstanding that this is the first day of April

title: A light hanging from a canoe-shaped bag
summary: A widely reprinted Omaha dispatch said a light had floated over Nebraska for months and was being hotly debated. Some described it hanging from a canoe-shaped bag, and rumour credited a German inventor. The story ran in at least sixteen papers.

title: A lighted object with rigging over Wilmington
summary: Hundreds of people on Wilmington's streets and wharves watched a brilliant floating mass move rapidly west of the city. Many said they could see a network like rigging around it. It was one of the few East Coast reports during the 1897 wave.

title: Chicago and Evanston stare at four lights
summary: On two nights, crowds in Chicago, Evanston and other lakeside towns watched a moving group of lights, white in front with green and smaller white lights on the sides. Evanston families gathered on Davis Field with telescopes and field glasses. Astronomers said the main light was a bright star.
quote: Men renowned for sobriety looked aloft through strong telescopes

title: Every station agent from West Liberty to Cedar Rapids
place: Burlington, Cedar Rapids and Northern line, eastern Iowa
summary: Hundreds of people in eastern Iowa reported the airship, and dispatches said every telegraph operator and station agent on the railroad between West Liberty and Cedar Rapids had seen it.

title: Topeka's airship was a kite
summary: Several hundred Topekans had watched an airship in the western sky one Saturday night. Weeks later the paper revealed it was a government experimental kite with two lanterns hung on it, sent up by a Mr. Patten.
hoax: Explained: a kite carrying two lanterns.

title: A snapshot of the airship at Rogers Park
summary: Walter McCann of Rogers Park said he photographed the airship at 5:30 one morning and showed two negatives, with three witnesses saying they saw him take them. Papers pointed out that modern photography could fake almost anything.
hoax: The photograph was widely judged a fake at the time.

title: Following the Hennepin canal
summary: A farmer named Karr living on the Rock River said he saw the airship following the Hennepin canal south of South Moline before dawn, heading west. The whole Moline police force swore they had seen it the night before.

title: Footprints where it landed near Red Cloud
summary: A dozen Red Cloud residents watched a large white light, some saying red and green too, travel northwest late on Monday night. Another account said the ship had landed in a field and that a party who reached the spot found a man's footprints.

title: A star that stopped to rest over St. Paul
summary: James Feeley, his family and other Marshall Avenue residents watched a light that looked like a star making a rapid trip and stopping now and then. Some thought they heard an order to cut away the anchor as it moved off.

title: A letter from the airship Pegasus
summary: A message said to have been dropped from the airship was found in a red stocking near Appleton. It named the craft Pegasus, and papers asked whether it was a canard.
hoax: Almost certainly a prank; the papers themselves suspected a canard.

title: A rabbi's story of a landing near Beaumont
summary: Rabbi A. Levy of Beaumont said the airship landed on a farm near his home one night, and that he went to the spot and heard what the travellers had told people there.

papers.paper: The Daily Morning Journal and Courier

title: Over the capital, then a kite at Fort Myer
summary: Hundreds of people in Columbia Heights watched what they took for the airship one night, and one report joked that it seemed ready to anchor on the Washington Monument. A week later, a crowd that thought they saw it over the Potomac learned they were watching an official aeroplane kite flown from Fort Myer.
hoax: The second sighting was explained as an Army experimental kite.

title: A strange light over Tacoma again
summary: Tacoma residents described a strange moving light in the night sky and took it for the airship that had been crossing the Midwest.

title: Settling on a meadow near Birmingham, Iowa
summary: William Walters and others said an airship settled onto a meadow a mile from town in the morning. As they ran toward it, it rose gracefully when they were 100 yards away. They described two men in the car and a machine about 100 feet long and 20 feet wide.
quote: Two men were plainly seen in the car.

title: An undertaker sees it fly down the beach
summary: Galveston undertaker Walter Norwood and his driver, Bob Tevis, said that at 3 a.m. under a bright moon they watched the airship follow the beach east, turn at the end of the island and follow the bay front. It was pointed at both ends, carried a headlight and looked like a big bird with regularly flapping wings.
quote: It looked like a great big bird, with wings flapping regularly

title: A message from three men lost in the sky
summary: Cripple Creek said the airship passed over on Sunday, and a man found a note on his barn roof claiming to come from three occupants, two Bostonians and a Frenchman, who had lost control and were drifting without water.
hoax: The papers treated the dropped message as a joke.

title: Sistersville signs an affidavit
summary: A mysterious light approached Sistersville from the northwest at about 9 p.m., stopped over Cochransville, Ohio, across the river and flashed red, white and green. Citizens signed an affidavit that they had seen it.

title: A huge cylinder flashing red fire
summary: Shortly before 5 o'clock, a crowd at Fourth and Market streets in Camden watched something in the western sky that looked like a huge cylinder flashing red fire, and many believed it was the airship.

title: Alexander Hamilton's stolen heifer
place: Near Le Roy, Woodson County, Kansas
summary: Former legislator Alexander Hamilton swore that an airship hovered over his farm, roped a three-year-old heifer and carried it off, and that the hide was found miles away the next day. Papers from Kansas to Utah printed his story.
hoax: Called "the champion lie" at the time; Hamilton was later reported to have made it up as a joke with friends.

title: The anchor at Merkel
summary: People coming home from church in Merkel said a heavy object on a rope was dragging along the ground until it caught on the railroad. Looking up, they saw the airship with lights shining from several windows. The anchor was said to be on display in town.
hoax: Generally treated as a tall tale.

title: A travelling salesman saw it four times
summary: George A. Williams, a travelling salesman for a large cloak firm, told Wheeling reporters he had seen the airship four times on his travels and had no doubt about it.

title: Woodcutters fight a hairy wild man near Rome, Ohio
place: Near Rome, Ohio (exact Rome not given)
summary: Weeks after a wild man frightened people near Rome, Ohio, two woodcutters, Charles Lukins and Bob Former, said they met him while cutting timber. After a hard struggle they drove the gorilla-like figure, which wore nothing but long curly hair, back into its retreat.
quote: He Wears Nothing but Hair, Which Is Long and Curly.

title: Passing over Ponca
summary: The mysterious airship was reliably reported to have passed over Ponca, according to a South Dakota paper across the Missouri.

title: Two lawmen interview an airship passenger
place: Bull Bayou, near Hot Springs, Arkansas
summary: Constable John Sumpter and deputy sheriff John McLemore swore an affidavit that near Bull Bayou at midnight they saw the airship land and talked with one of its crew, who said it had come down for water.

title: A white serpent off the New England coast
place: At sea between Gay Head and Winter Quarter lightship
summary: Officers and passengers of the Merchants and Miners steamer Gloucester, bound from Boston to Baltimore, said they saw a white sea serpent 40 to 45 feet long early one Sunday morning, off the coast near Gay Head.

title: A wild woman who leaps fences like a deer
place: Near Elkins, Randolph County, West Virginia
summary: Farmers near Elkins said a wild woman crossed their fields and was too fast to catch, leaping fences like a deer. At night they heard hideous noises like a dog's or fox's bark, and searchers from Elkins scoured the woods without finding her.

title: A golden eagle attacks a woman in her garden
summary: A widely reprinted item said a great golden eagle swooped on Mrs. Jane Mortenson as she bent over in her garden near Honey Creek, sank its talons into her back and tried to lift her, and that she died of the shock the next day.

title: The steamer Shark meets a 100-foot serpent
place: Off Pumpkin Rock, near Boothbay Harbor, Maine
summary: Captain Handy McKown's fishing steamer Shark, returning from herring fishing near Pumpkin Rock, passed an immense sea serpent 80 to 100 feet long with a head four feet across, swimming with part of its neck out of the water.

title: A wild man caught asleep in the Nebraska pines
place: Pine forests of Dawes and Sioux counties, Nebraska
summary: A wild man who had haunted the pine forests of Dawes and Sioux counties was captured while asleep. He seemed to know nothing when the insanity board examined him.

title: A white serpent with a horse's head off Block Island
summary: Block Island sailors and fishermen reported a white sea serpent with a horse-like head and great brown eyes. The New York Sun noted that three separate sources had described a white serpent that season.
quote: Its Head Is Like That of a Horse and It Has Great Brown Eyes

title: Joe Downey's Lake Michigan serpent
place: Lake Michigan beach, North Chicago, Illinois
summary: Joe Downey of North Chicago said his family was on the beach at dusk when two men in bathing suits ran past yelling about something in Lake Michigan. They then saw the creature themselves. Chicago papers called it Joe Downey's sea serpent.
quote: Have you seen it?

title: A flat head beside the boat off Salem
summary: Two summer visitors fishing near a buoy off Salem said a large flat head rose out of the water next to their boat, followed by a long body.

title: A girl saves her cousin from an eagle
summary: A Pennsylvania paper said Bertha Moore fought off an eagle that went for her small cousin, Elsie Talsen, while they walked on a mountainside near Germania.

papers.place: Lake Providence, East Carroll Parish, La.

title: A sea serpent in Lake Wawasee
summary: Hotel guests and cottagers at Lake Wawasee said they had seen and heard a serpent in the lake. The Indianapolis Journal joked that the resort could now rank with the seaside attractions.
hoax: Written half in jest as resort publicity.

title: A mysterious light over Tombstone
summary: At about 9:30 one night, people in Tombstone noticed a mysterious light in the sky. The Prospector said it did not want to start another flying-machine theory, but recorded the mystery anyway.

title: A Sunday school superintendent sees it dance
summary: Three Hartford men fishing on Long Island Sound, one of them a Sunday school superintendent, said an all-black sea serpent passed their boat, writhed about and then vanished. The paper reported it in a teasing tone.

papers.paper: The Daily Morning Journal and Courier.

title: The wild man of the White Plains road
place: Between Mount Vernon, Bronxville and White Plains, New York
summary: Cyclists on the road between Mount Vernon and White Plains reported a wild man who burst out of the woods to stop travellers, and a lawyer said he met him at the foot of a hill. Weeks later the Bronxville wild man was back, chasing passers-by and frightening women and girls in the Masterton woods.

papers.paper: The Daily Morning Journal and Courier

title: A noisy light on the Marine Hospital lawns
place: Marine Hospital grounds, Staten Island, New York
summary: A sober old waterman named Lindsey and his dog said they saw a strange light moving across the Marine Hospital lawns between Stapleton and Clifton on Staten Island, and heard sounds with it.

title: Two sea serpents at once off Greenport
place: North of Greenport, Long Island, New York
summary: C. Edwards Stauson, a Greenport drug clerk, came back from a morning's fishing on Long Island Sound with no fish and a story of two sea serpents, each about fifty feet long, swimming together north of Greenport.
hoax: The papers ran it as a fish story.

title: A locomotive engineer's light in the sky
place: Eastern Minnesota railway, between Duluth and St. Paul
summary: John J. Hussey, engineer of the day train down from Duluth on the Eastern Minnesota, reported a strange light in the heavens that people supposed was an airship, months after the main wave had ended.

title: Swampscott fishermen row for their lives
summary: A fisherman reached shore exhausted from rowing and said a serpent had come at his dory off Pig Rocks: long, scaly, barnacled and whitish, with a seal-like head, fangs and hissing breath. Two others said they had rowed in so hard from the same thing a day or two earlier that they fainted on the sand.

title: A thing with arms rises off Ship John Light
place: Delaware Bay off Ship John Shoal Light, near Bayside, New Jersey
summary: Three sturgeon fishermen said a black creature with a lighter face reared eight feet out of the water a few feet from their boat, and that arms came out about three feet below its shoulders. One of them quit fishing and went home to Salem, and several boats were short of crew.

title: A serpent blamed for the vanished menhaden
summary: When the menhaden (pogy) fleet couldn't find a single school along the New England coast, the crew of a small Canadian smack insisted they had seen, sober and in daylight, a serpent over 60 feet long and as thick as a keg of nails, lashing the water to foam and carrying off the fish.

title: The Leeds Devil returns to the Pines
place: The Pine Barrens near Vincentown, New Jersey
summary: Pine Barrens folk said the Leeds Devil, not clearly seen since it supposedly warned of the Civil War, was back: two men in separate settlements reported it at about the same time. Locals took it as an omen of disaster.

title: Champ off Split Rock, 80 feet long
place: Lake Champlain between the Vermont shore and Split Rock
summary: A witness the Burlington News called entirely trustworthy saw a creature about 80 feet long swimming south half a mile away, where the lake is deepest. Its head was broad and flat like a hand on a table, its body a low arch and its broad tail tip stuck up out of the water. It sank in a boil of bubbles.

title: A seven-foot hairy giant at a farmhouse window
place: Sam Crooks farm, four miles from Diagonal, Iowa
summary: Two women at a farmhouse near Diagonal looked up when the window went dark and saw a man-shaped being nearly seven feet tall, so overgrown with long black hair that no features showed. The mother fainted in the yard, and the creature stepped over her and blocked her daughter, who was carrying the baby. Days later a hired man near Macksburg said a hairy giant like a big ape chased him.

title: A flying monster on Stansbury Island
place: Stansbury Island, Great Salt Lake, Utah
summary: Two hunters back from Stansbury Island described a 60-foot creature like a fish, an alligator and a bat combined, at home in the air, on the beach and in the salt water. They said they watched it for three days.
hoax: The paper printed it under the headline "A prize yarn".

title: A seven-foot wild man in Coos County
summary: Ranchers and miners in the Coos County mountains reported a wild man about seven feet tall who had been shot at twice and missed. They organized a hunt, and the papers guessed he was a giant prospector who had lost his mind.
quote: seven feet tall, muscular and unkempt

title: The hairy 'wild man of the Sixes' shakes miners' cabins
place: Mining camps on the Sixes River, Curry County, Oregon
summary: Miners on the Sixes River said the hairy wild man they had long feared was back, seen three times in a month. At night it shook the corner of one cabin and the door of another, and a miner named Ward fired at it as it walked away and missed. Earlier reports said it threw rocks like baseballs.

title: A sheep-headed animal in the Rock River
place: Rock River at Sterling and Rock Falls, Illinois
summary: Hundreds of people watched a glossy, dark animal with a head like a sheep's play in the Rock River by the bridge all day. Papers compared it to Big Ben, a sea lion that had escaped into Lake Michigan and been reported in the Mississippi that winter, which is the likely answer.

title: A schoolman fights an unknown animal on the prairie
place: Prairie north of Miller, Hand County, South Dakota
summary: Professor J. H. Snoddy, 65, out at night looking for his horse, sat down on what he took for a rock, and it sprang at his throat. He fought it off six times with a bridle and a penknife on the way home. It stood as tall as a man on its hind legs and left tooth marks on the iron bit; he thought it might be a mountain lion.

title: A striped serpent beside the tug Thompson
summary: The crew of the tug Thompson, fishing after towing out a schooner, said a serpent of olive green with turquoise and bright red stripes, two rows of teeth and flashing eyes came within two feet of the boat. The captain's wife gave the colours.

title: Three women see a serpent in Devils Lake
place: Devils Lake, by the Chautauqua grounds, North Dakota
summary: Three women walking the beach by the Chautauqua grounds saw, through opera glasses, a great snake-headed animal covered in black scales swimming toward the north shore, leaving a trail of foam. Armed men patrolled the shore afterward, and a group of Native people said they had seen it earlier that day.

title: A horse-headed swimmer in Raritan Bay
place: Raritan Bay off South Amboy, New Jersey
summary: Fishing early in the morning, J. B. Edwards saw what he took for a man swimming toward his boat from the Staten Island shore. It had a head something like a horse's, circled the boat two or three times and vanished.

title: The Delaware County 'gorilla'
place: Darby and Sharon Hill, Delaware County, Pennsylvania
summary: For weeks people around Darby said a dark-haired, ape-like thing that ran upright and then on all fours jumped out at them on country roads. In April a Philadelphia detective said it was a disturbed local man wearing a bearskin, his hair smeared with phosphorus.
hoax: A detective said it was a man in a bearskin.

title: An 'enormous ape' on the Laurel Run road
place: Mountain road between Georgetown and Laurel Run, near Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania
summary: People on the mountain road between Georgetown and Laurel Run fled from an animal that came out of the brush. Some said it was an enormous ape; others said a bear down from the Bear Creek woods.

title: Blazing eyes in a Lamberton barnyard
place: Farms around Lamberton, and later Mankato, Minnesota
summary: Something killed sheep and a colt around Lamberton; the local vet saw two blazing eyes and a huge shadowy shape and galloped off to rouse the neighbours. Days later near Mankato a steer was found with its back torn open, and papers decided the culprit was a mountain lion.

title: A 100-foot monster snaps a propeller off Ocean City
place: Atlantic Ocean about seven miles off Ocean City, New Jersey
summary: The captain of a fishing launch said that while they looked over a wreck offshore, they hit a monster about 100 feet long that tore away their propeller. It blew like a whale, but its spout was blood red. He and his crew of six offered to swear to it.

title: A horned 'young sea serpent' in the Long Beach surf
place: Surf in front of the Long Beach bathhouse, California
summary: Something about fifteen feet long with three horn-like bristles on its head and a tail split into three barbed points played in the breakers in front of the lifesaving station for half an hour, leaping half out of the water twice.

title: A cone of light that drifted around a farmhouse
summary: On a dark, misty night a cone-shaped light as big as a corn shock moved like a skiff on waves from a vacant cabin to a neighbour's house, hung there fifteen minutes, came closer and seemed to have something dark like a person inside. Three named neighbours wrote to the paper asking what it was.

title: A huge eagle tries to carry off a boy
place: Near Confluence, Braxton County, West Virginia
summary: A merchant's eight-year-old son was playing a little way from his father and brother when a bald eagle, said to be the biggest ever seen there, swooped on him. The boy tore loose and screamed, and the bird flew off to the mountains.

title: A serpent in Walker Lake, Nevada
summary: An engineer said he watched a black, square-headed animal tear through Walker Lake throwing spray for ten minutes. Later two miners said they rowed toward what looked like a man in a skin and saw a creature they put at 80 feet long. The papers noted that Paiute people by the lake had long spoken of one.

title: A 40-foot snake throws a farmer twenty feet
place: Near Ages Lake, east of Valley, Nebraska
summary: Two farmers walking through tall grass to bathe in a lake said a snake 40 feet long and a foot thick rose under one of them, threw him twenty feet and broke two ribs, then charged off to the lake bellowing like a bull. Locals had told of a big snake there for twenty years.

title: A captain swears on his Bible to a serpent
place: Surf off Cornfield Point light, Old Saybrook, Connecticut
summary: Captain Jim Sherman of the Annie D. said he saw a sea serpent with a head like an alligator's, several feet around, in the surf off Cornfield Point. When friends laughed he pulled out a pocket Bible and swore to it; he said it headed for Long Island.

title: Hoof prints in the snow across South Jersey
place: Camden, Gloucester and Burlington counties, New Jersey
summary: A Philadelphia dispatch reported clear two-legged, hoof-like tracks in the crust of the snow, which had turned scores of towns in Camden, Gloucester and Burlington counties into places where women and children were afraid to go out after dark. The writer said he had meant to make fun of the Leeds Devil but found the fear too real.
quote: the footprints of a two-legged beast or bird, shod with steel

title: A red neck through the dining-room window
summary: A Vineland correspondent wrote that Moses Carter was reading in his dining room when the creature smashed the window and pushed in a long, bright red neck, with eyes like arc lamps and a three-pronged tongue. The story was played for thrills.
quote: It had eyes the size of arc lamps
hoax: Told with obvious exaggeration; treat it as a tall tale.

title: Tracks at Groveville, Trenton and Mount Holly
place: Trenton and Mount Holly, New Jersey
summary: Harry Clymer of Groveville found hoof prints in his back yard, and Clarence Williams saw similar tracks in Trenton's City Park. Both said they looked like a small horse's, but in pairs with gaps that suggested great leaps. At Mount Holly an elderly citizen, William Cronk, said the Leeds Devil had landed in his back yard.

title: Now called the flying hoof
summary: From Burlington came word that the creature, now nicknamed the flying hoof and given horse's legs and enormous wings, was still being reported by sober citizens. A New Yorker claimed it had escaped from his shop, and the National Museum's bat expert said he had seen worse things between midnight and sunrise.

title: The devil shot in a Smyrna stable yard
summary: After Jersey Devil tracks were found in the snow in two Mount Vernon Street yards, a stable driver in Smyrna was persuaded the creature was in the transportation company's yard and shot it. The Smyrna Times reported it as a joke played on him.
hoax: A practical joke, as the paper itself said.

title: A wild man on Prospect Hill
summary: Scores of residents in north Taunton asked the police to investigate a wild man who roamed the edge of the woods near Prospect Hill and appeared by the roads. Mothers kept their children indoors.

title: Milton remembers a one-footed devil
summary: A Milton correspondent said the New Jersey visitor was surely the same devil that came to Sussex County near the Drawbridge about 34 years earlier. That one had a single shod foot and left tracks in the snow around a farmer's haystacks.

title: Paterson police chase a devil-bat
summary: Early one morning a Paterson police sergeant wired headquarters that the devil-bat had been found. The reserves were rushed to West Paterson, where officers and a dozen citizens hunted through the woods behind a sanitarium after hair-raising shrieks were heard near an old mill. A streetcar motorman described the thing.
quote: We have found the devil-bat

title: The wild man with an axe
summary: For weeks, a mysterious man carrying an axe and a gun camped in barns and haystacks across northern Johnson County. He burrowed a den in one farmer's hay loft and frightened people near Valley City.

title: An eagle tries to carry off a girl
summary: Josiah Olmtree, a farmer on the edge of the Adirondacks, said a huge eagle that had been raiding his sheep's feed swooped on his eight-year-old daughter in the yard, and he barely saved her.

title: A museum man admits the publicity stunt
place: Ninth and Arch Museum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania
summary: Papers reported that a Philadelphia showman named Hope had spread rumours of the beast to promote a so-called Australian vampire on show at the Ninth and Arch Museum, and that the sightings everywhere were imaginary.
hoax: Reported at the time as a museum publicity stunt.

title: Long Beach fishermen meet a 40-foot serpent
summary: Guy Griffith, James Harvey and three other fishermen in the launch Reta said that some miles off the coast they saw a sea serpent 40 feet long, with a brown head as big as a small barrel, eyes like a man's fist and a large dorsal fin, swinging its head like a snake. Papers noted that Long Beach was a dry town.

title: A giant crane attacks two fishermen
place: Back River, off Twin Oaks Shore, Maryland
summary: A deputy sheriff and a wrestler known as Americus said a giant crane attacked their boat after midnight while they were fishing on Back River, just as the deputy was landing a big eel. They fought it off.

title: Arbutus hunters meet a hoofed thing
place: Woods three miles west of Seaford, Delaware
summary: Five young Seaford men out picking arbutus in the woods west of town said a queer, dog-like animal about two feet tall, with large hoofs, came out of a brush pile. Papers called it the Jersey Devil.

title: Captain Doughty captures the devil
summary: Captain George Doughty was said to have overpowered the Jersey Devil just outside Atlantic City after it attacked him. It turned out to be a huge bird of unknown species, with claws like a vulture's, feathers like an albatross's and a parrot's beak, and it was put on exhibition.

title: Spring Valley's posse hunts the devil bird
summary: Armed men searched the hills and swamps around Spring Valley for the Jersey devil bird, or bombat, described as having an immense head, a small hairy body and arms with web-like skin. Locals refused to believe the Atlantic City capture.

title: The airship over the Salton Sea was a mirage
summary: At twilight, people in Imperial and Brawley watched for an aeroplane seen the night before cruising over the Salton Sea, and some guessed at a secret aircraft factory in the San Jacinto wilds. Within days, papers reported it had been a mirage.
hoax: Explained at the time as a mirage.

title: Northbridge hunts its ghost light
summary: For several nights at about the same hour, a light ranging from the size of a bulb to a bushel basket appeared on a high ledge near Northbridge, climbing trees and hills and then vanishing into a pond. Treated as a joke at first, it frightened scores of children, and the whole village turned out to hunt it.

title: A horned terror in Greenwood Lake
place: Greenwood Lake, New Jersey and New York
summary: Three Montclair men back from Greenwood Lake said a queer amphibious creature with a horn and a sponge-like tail speared a bass, soaked them and tried to climb into their boat. One showed a slashed wrist as proof.

title: San Francisco Bay's airship was Venus and Jupiter
summary: For two days, Bay Area residents reported an airship's lights swinging across the sky a few hundred feet up. Astronomer R. Tracy Crawford of the University of California said the two lights were Venus and Jupiter.
hoax: Explained by an astronomer: the planets Venus and Jupiter.

title: The Walker Lake monster
summary: Visitors to Walker Lake had long reported a monster serpent or prehistoric beast in the desert lake, and several mining men claimed to have seen it. A new account came via a Reno police captain's brother, mining at Lucky Boy. A Tonopah paper headlined it as Reno booze at work.
hoax: The paper's headline blamed the drink.

title: The Jersey Devil found dead
summary: In October, a Burlington story said the carcass of the Jersey Devil had been found fresh in the woods. Reprints in at least a dozen papers described it as a blend of sea serpent, kangaroo, bobcat and "Jersey lightning" (applejack).
hoax: Written as a joke; one paper said it was a small kangaroo.

title: Bowdoinham's ghost house and phantom light
summary: A widely reprinted Maine item said Bowdoinham had a house where the chairs gathered in groups at midnight, a cane that tapped from room to room by itself, a phantom light and a mystic woodchuck.
hoax: Local ghost lore, written for fun.

title: A Worcester man says he flew to New York by night
summary: Wallace E. Tillinghast, a Worcester manufacturing executive, told reporters he had secretly built a three-seat monoplane, flown it at night to New York, circled the Statue of Liberty at 4,000 feet and returned via Boston. He refused to show the machine. His claim set off a wave of night-light sightings across New England.
hoax: No such aircraft was ever produced; historians treat the claim as a hoax.

title: An immigration officer sees lights over Boston Harbor
summary: Arthur W. Hoe of the US immigration station, woken by whistles in Boston Harbor, said he saw the dark frame of an aircraft with lights fly against the wind past him, heard the whir of an engine and watched the lights recede.

title: Thousands watch an airship circle Worcester
summary: Shortly before 6 p.m., a light appeared over Worcester, hovered, left and came back to circle the city four times, sweeping a powerful searchlight over the crowds. Thousands filled the streets. Tillinghast was out of town, and the story ran in more than forty papers.
quote: sweeping the heavens with a searchlight of tremendous power

papers.paper: Newark Evening Star and Newark Advertiser.

title: Lights over the villages east of Worcester
summary: After the Tillinghast story, people along the route from Webster to Danielson, Connecticut, and as far as Boston Common said they too had seen mysterious lights crossing the night sky.

title: A dog-killing beast in Highland Park
place: Highland Park and Chelsea Hill, Richmond, Virginia
summary: Residents of Highland Park, Chelsea Hill and Maddox Hill talked of forming an armed posse after a mysterious animal killed dogs, hogs and at least one cow. A girl who saw it in the bushes said it was bigger than a dog, with a bushy tail.

title: The 'gorilla' of the South Mountain
place: Near Pen Mar and Rouzerville, on the Maryland-Pennsylvania line
summary: For weeks papers reported a big ape, said to have escaped from a circus, in the mountains of southern Pennsylvania. A man walking through a field between Pen Mar and Rouzerville said he saw it in bright sunshine, and it was reported again near Dam No. 4 on the Potomac.

title: 'The terror' of Hanover Farms
place: Hanover Farms, near Browns Mills, New Jersey
summary: A night animal that attacked dogs and frightened horses and cattle had mothers warning children that "the terror" would get them. Hunters reading its tracks guessed a small bear or a catamount, and two dogs that trailed it into a swamp came back yelping and would not track again.

title: A farmer kills the Queen Anne's County 'gorilla'
place: Walnut Ridge farm, near Centreville, Queen Anne's County, Maryland
summary: After days of stories about a ferocious "gorilla" near Centreville, a farmer killed it on his land. Rumour said he choked it with his bare hands; he said he shot it, and thought it was a cross between a bulldog and a Newfoundland.

title: A white-furred phantom beast near English
place: East of English, Crawford County, Indiana
summary: People east of English said an animal about three feet high with dull white fur, howling like a frightened fox, killed a farmer's cow and pig. Everyone who saw it ran, so nobody could describe it well, and farmers carried pitchforks or guns into the woods.

title: A shot 'gorilla' gets up and chases a man in Gettysburg
summary: A woman on York Street saw a creature about four feet high moving along her back fence. A neighbour fired a shotgun and it dropped, but when he walked over it jumped up on its hind legs and chased him into the house, then headed off toward Biglerville.

title: The Alkali Lake monster of Hay Springs
place: Alkali Lake (Walgren Lake), six miles southeast of Hay Springs, Nebraska
summary: People near Hay Springs said a creature about 20 feet long and as thick as a man lived in the alkali lake southeast of town, spouting water 20 feet high with a hiss like a locomotive. Bathers stopped going in and locals planned to catch it.

title: A puppy-faced 'water dog' bumps swimmers at Yankton
place: Where the James River meets the Missouri, near Yankton, South Dakota
summary: Swimmers said they ran into a four-foot animal with a puppy's head, small ears, a blunt snout, fiery eyes, a grey back, yellow belly and broad heavy tail. Fishermen called it a water dog; others thought it was an otter.

title: A circus ape blamed in Elk Grove
summary: Farmers around Elk Grove drove their children to school after reports of a huge ape, said to have escaped from a circus at Platteville that summer, and blamed it for killing a cow. Hunters found nothing.
